script: A1 Approved before implementation (an emergency change: by the emergency approver before it is made, and by the CAB within 2 working days)
A3 Rollback plan covering every component the change alters
A4 Post-implementation review recorded within 5 working days

rows: The product owner writes each feature as a user story. For a story that touches sign-in, payment or customer data, the security acceptance criteria are taken from the Group's application security checklist (SITL-POL-012); the checklist has no card-payment items. The Security Architecture & Standards Manager approves the criteria at sprint planning.
The story, with its security criteria and their approval
Product owner; Security Architecture & Standards Manager
A design change that alters a data flow or an integration is reviewed against the portal team's engineering principles before it is built. A design that fails goes back to the team.

Developers work on branches. Each merge request is reviewed by a second developer against the secure coding essentials (SITL-POL-012 Section 7.1). The build runs a static code scan and a check of the open-source libraries; a High finding stops the build unless the Manila development lead waives it, and the waiver tool has no field for a reason.
Merge request reviews; scan reports; waivers

Each release is deployed to the QA environment. Functional tests run, then the Group security test gate (SITL-POL-012 Section 6.1): a dynamic scan and tests of sign-in and session handling. The product owner signs off acceptance.
Test runs (TR-…) attached to the release ticket; acceptance sign-off

The release's RFC goes to the weekly Change Advisory Board with its test evidence and rollback plan (SITL-POL-009 Section 6.1). Before running the release job, the release engineer checks by hand that the RFC is approved: the job itself does not check.
The RFC and its approval in the IT service management tool
The release job deploys to production on Wednesday at 21:00, Manila time. It is the only deployment path the pipeline has.

Each month the database administrator copies the production portal database into QA, on the Manila development lead's approval of a request under the portal team's own refresh procedure, which has no masking step: end-customers' names, addresses and account numbers are copied as they are, and the old copy is overwritten at the next refresh.
The refresh request and its approval
Within 5 working days of a release, the change owner records in the RFC whether the change worked and caused no incident.
The post-implementation review in the RFC

Development, QA and production each run in a cloud account of their own. The nine developers still hold write access to the production database, granted in 2025 for hotfixes, and sign in to it with their development accounts.
Cloud account and database access lists
sdlc.note: The customer portal's delivery pipeline at the Manila office, as the Manila development lead described it on 30 November 2026. The portal is built in-house by nine developers; it lets end-customers of Manila's clients see their accounts and support tickets, and pay by card.

Partly: it does some of it, or not every time
No: nothing at the stage does it
gates: Security requirements set for each feature from its risks, laws and contracts, card payments included, and approved before it is built
Secure system architecture and engineering principles
Each design change reviewed against the engineering principles before it is built
Code peer-reviewed and scanned before merge, and each serious finding fixed or accepted with a recorded reason
Security testing in development and acceptance
Security tests of each release, with results recorded, before acceptance
Separation of development, test and production environments
Development, test and production kept apart, with no developer able to change production outside the release path
An approved RFC, with test evidence and a rollback plan, before the release runs
Production personal data masked or removed before it is copied into QA, and the copy deleted after testing
